question: Does this bank offer a Kisan Credit Card scheme?
reference: SBI Kisan Credit Card (KCC) SBI's Kisan Credit Card interest rate, eligibility, and loan limit — the scheme provides timely and adequate credit to farmers to meet cultivation (production credit) needs plus contingency…
answer: Yes. SBI offers a Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme. The KCC provides farmers with timely credit for cultivation and contingency expenses, with interest rates ranging from 7 % per annum for loans up to ₹3 lakh (subject to government subvention) to 3.25 % above the 1‑Year MCLR for amounts between ₹3 lakh and ₹50 lakh, and a credit‑risk‑based rate for larger amounts. The scheme also offers a 3 % prompt‑repayment incentive for loans up to ₹3 lakh that are repaid on time.
retrieved_contexts: SBI Kisan Credit Card (KCC) SBI's Kisan Credit Card interest rate, eligibility, and loan limit — the scheme provides timely and adequate credit to farmers to meet cultivation (production credit) needs plus contingency expenses. Eligibility: - Individual owner cultivators. - Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and share croppers. - Self-Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers. Loan Amount: Need-based, determined by the cropping pattern, acreage, and the District Level Technical Committee's Scale of Finance (SOF) for the crop — no fixed minimum or maximum ceiling is stated. Interest Rate: - Up to Rs. 3 lakh: 7% p.a., subject to Government of India interest subvention. - Above Rs. 3 lakh to below Rs. 50 lakh: 3.25% above the 1-Year MCLR. - Rs. 50 lakh and above: priced per the borrower's Credit Risk Assessment (CRA) rating. - An additional 3% interest subvention applies as a Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) on loans up to Rs. 3 lakh repaid on time, effectively lowering the cost further for prompt-paying farmers. Margin: Nil. Security / Collateral: - Primary security: hypothecation of crops grown / assets created out of the loan. - Collateral is waived for limits up to Rs. 2 lakh (or up to Rs. 3 lakh under a tie-up arrangement). - Above these thresholds: equitable or registered mortgage of land, valued at 100% of the loan amount, is required. Repayment: Aligned to the crop's cultivation and marketing cycle (short-duration or long-duration crop, as applicable) — not a fixed EMI schedule. Tenure: 5 years, with the sanctioned limit eligible for a 10% annual increase, subject to periodic review. Additional Benefits: - RuPay Kisan Credit Card (debit card) issued against the account. - Optional Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) crop insurance. - Optional personal accident and health insurance cover.

question: Does this bank offer a Kisan Credit Card scheme?
reference: Punjab National Bank — Kisan Credit Card / PNB Krishi Card (Agriculture Loan) Purpose: A revolving credit facility for farmers to meet short-term crop production and allied agricultural needs, under the Kisan Credit…
answer: Yes. Punjab National Bank offers the Kisan Credit Card, marketed as the PNB Krishi Card. It is a revolving credit facility for farmers to meet short‑term crop production and allied agricultural needs. The card provides loans up to ₹50 lakh, with interest rates that vary by loan size and are subject to the government’s interest‑subvention scheme. Eligibility covers a wide range of farmers, including owner‑cultivators, tenants, lessees, and even landless labourers or share‑croppers on affidavit alone. The card is valid for five years from the sanction date.
retrieved_contexts: Punjab National Bank — Kisan Credit Card / PNB Krishi Card (Agriculture Loan) Purpose: A revolving credit facility for farmers to meet short-term crop production and allied agricultural needs, under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme that PNB implements as PNB Krishi Card. Interest Rate: Regular crop loans up to Rs. 3 lakh (including KCC) are reported at around 7% p.a. — this reflects the government's Interest Subvention Scheme for short-term crop loans, under which the effective rate to a prompt-repaying farmer can be lower still via an additional Prompt Repayment Incentive. For loans up to Rs. 20 lakh (covering KCC/crop loans above Rs. 3 lakh), reported pricing is Base Rate + 2%, with PNB's reported Base Rate at approximately 9.6%. Government Interest Subvention: Farmers availing KCC-based short-term crop loans are eligible for interest subvention under the government scheme, which reduces the effective borrowing cost below the bank's card rate — the exact subvention percentage and prompt-repayment incentive should be confirmed as they are set by government policy, not the bank alone. Eligibility (per PNB's own official Krishi Card scheme document): Progressive literate and illiterate farmers who are owner cultivators, tenants, lessee or allottee farmers with recorded occupancy rights, or farmers with ancestral/perpetual cultivation rights, plus Joint Liability Groups (JLGs). Oral tenants are eligible only if the landowner agrees to become a co-borrower — except where the account is secured by liquid securities (FDR/NSC/KVP), in which case no co-borrower is required. Landless labourers, share croppers, tenant farmers, and oral lessees can be issued a PNB Krishi Card up to Rs. 50,000 on the basis of an affidavit alone. Extent of Loan: Maximum Rs. 50 lakh. Credit Limit (how PNB calculates the sanctioned amount): First-year short-term limit = Scale of Finance for the crop (as decided by the District Level Technical Committee) x extent of area cultivated, plus 10% of that limit toward post-harvest/household/ consumption needs (health insurance premium coverable up to Rs. 3 lakh), plus 20% toward repairs and maintenance of farm assets, plus crop/PAIS/asset insurance. Each subsequent year (2nd-5th) adds a further 10% for cost escalation, plus an estimated term-loan component for investments (land development, minor irrigation, farm equipment). The 5th-year short-term limit plus the estimated long-term requirement becomes the Maximum Permissible Limit (MPL) — this MPL is the actual Kisan Credit Card limit. Margin: Nil for crop loans under the Krishi Card Scheme. Security: Up to Rs. 1

question: Does this bank offer a Kisan Credit Card scheme?
reference: Kotak Mahindra Bank Kisan Credit Card Purpose: A revolving credit facility for farmers' cultivation and allied agricultural credit needs, under the nationwide Kisan Credit Card scheme — aimed at providing hassle-free,…
answer: Yes. Kotak Mahindra Bank offers a Kisan Credit Card scheme. It is marketed as a revolving credit facility for farmers’ cultivation and allied agricultural needs, called the “Crop Loan.” The Kisan Credit Card serves as the working‑capital component, while a separate Agri Term Loan covers medium‑term requirements such as land development, irrigation and farm assets. The product is available to all farmers who are owner‑cultivators, with eligibility criteria and interest rates detailed on the bank’s own product page.
retrieved_contexts: Kotak Mahindra Bank Kisan Credit Card Purpose: A revolving credit facility for farmers' cultivation and allied agricultural credit needs, under the nationwide Kisan Credit Card scheme — aimed at providing hassle-free, timely credit support through a single-window facility for cultivation and other farming-related needs. Kotak calls this product "Crop Loan," with the Kisan Credit Card as its working-capital component and a separate Agri Term Loan for medium-term needs (land development, irrigation, farm assets). Eligibility (from Kotak's own eligibility page): All Farmers — Individuals or Joint borrowers who are owner cultivators. Minimum age 21, maximum age 65 at loan tenure end; if the primary borrower is over 65, a co-borrower within the normal age range must be included. Credit Limit: The working-capital (KCC) limit is fixed based on the Scale of Finance (SOF) for the crops grown on the borrower's land, with an annual review; the limit is renewed after 5 years. The separate Agri Term Loan component runs for a maximum fixed term of 5 years. Interest Rate: Prevailing MCLR/reference rate at the low end, up to a stated maximum of 24% p.a. depending on the borrower's profile. Charges (from Kotak's own fees-and-charges page): processing fee up to 2% of the sanctioned limit; documentation charge Rs. 5,000; credit administration charge 1% of the sanctioned limit; supervision/crop verification Rs. 750-3,000 every 6 months depending on limit size; penal charge 8% p.a. on overdue amounts. Validity: Kisan Credit Card working-capital limit is renewed after 5 years, with an annual review in between. Honest gap: Kotak's own pages state processing fees and other charges in detail but do not publish a specific Margin percentage or a rupee-threshold collateral/security requirement for the Crop Loan/KCC — unlike PNB, BOI, Indian Bank, or Bank of Maharashtra, whose own pages do state these. Not inferred or borrowed from another bank's rules; confirm the current margin and security requirement directly with Kotak or a nearest branch.

Offers 250+ features including balance checks, transaction history, statement downloads, bill payments, shopping, investments, credit card management, personal loan applications, and fixed deposit account opening, all from within one app. A "Pay Your Contact" feature lets users send money using just a mobile number. UPI (via Kotak811): Registration for Kotak811 UPI enables instant money transfers and bill payments. Secured via advanced encryption and biometric authentication. Confirm current app features and UPI limits with the bank, since these are periodically revised by NPCI/RBI guidance as well as bank policy.

This is a summary of publicly listed Kotak Mahindra Bank scheme names — exact current rates, minimum amounts, and eligibility should be confirmed with the bank before advising a customer.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's education loan is an unsecured loan of up to Rs. 75 lakh for higher studies, offered through its "Education Loans from Credila" program — a tie-up with Credila Financial Services, a dedicated education-loan NBFC, rather than a loan Kotak underwrites directly in-house. As of March 2024, Credila had funded 178,000+ Indian students across 63 countries and 4,600+ institutes under this partnership. Loan Amount: Unsecured loan up to Rs. 75 lakh. Collateral Options: - Moveable/liquid collateral, such as a fixed deposit. - Immovable collateral, such as a flat, house, bungalow, non-agricultural land, or shop. Special Benefits: - Tax benefits under Section 80E of the Income Tax Act. - Seamless loan sanctions. - NIL TCS (Tax Collected at Source) on foreign remittance. - Up to 100% financing, covering tuition fee and ancillary expenses. Eligibility: Applicant and co-applicant(s) must meet Credila's own credit and underwriting norms, applicable from time to time. Sanctioning is at Credila's sole discretion, not Kotak Mahindra Bank's. Note: because this is a third-party-administered partnership product rather than a Kotak-underwritten loan, exact interest rates, tenure, and processing fees are set by Credila and should be confirmed on Credila's own terms before quoting a rate to a customer.
